paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of examples and the minADE20 value for two different methods. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Examples" and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 8, with tick marks at integer values. The y-axis is labeled "minADE20 ( )" and has a linear scale ranging from 15.0 to 18.0, with tick marks at 0.5 intervals. The first line, colored orange and marked with circles, represents "Random"; it begins at approximately 17.9 when the number of examples is 0, declines to approximately 16.8 at an example number of 2, and then stabilizes around 16.6 for the remainder of the x-axis, ending at approximately 16.6 when the number of examples is 8. The second line, colored blue and marked with circles, represents "ST-ES"; it begins at approximately 17.1 when the number of examples is 0, declines to approximately 15.5 at an example number of 2, and then plateaus around 15.6 for the remainder of the x-axis, ending at approximately 15.6 when the number of examples is 8.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of examples and the minADE20 value for two different methods. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 8, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “minADE20 ( )” and displays a linear scale from 15.0 to 18.0, with tick labels at 0.5 intervals. A blue line, labeled “ST-ES”, is present, marked with circular data points, and begins at approximately 17.1 at an x-value of 0. The line declines steadily to a value of approximately 15.4 at an x-value of 2, and then remains relatively constant, fluctuating between approximately 15.4 and 15.6 for the remainder of the x-axis range, ending at approximately 15.6 at an x-value of 8. An orange line, labeled “Random”, also marked with circular data points, starts at approximately 17.8 at an x-value of 0, decreasing to approximately 17.1 at an x-value of 2, continuing to approximately 16.9 at an x-value of 4, then increasing slightly to approximately 17.0 at an x-value of 8.
